note: Expectations recorded by hand from queries reviewed during development. 'auto' fields are checked mechanically by run_evals.py; 'review' fields are for a human reading the SQL, because they cannot be verified from text alone.

questions.question: What is the Ad eCPM (USD) trend?

review.denominator: ad impressions, not sessions or users
traps: no date filter at all - 'trend' states no period
fact_user_daily already stores ad_revenue_usd and ad_impressions, so no COUNTIF on a guessed ad_event_type value is needed

questions.question: What is the D7 retention by country for installs in the last 30 days?

review.denominator: cohort size fixed at install, not users active in the window
traps: fact_retention_daily looks right but has NO country column, so it cannot answer this
cohorts younger than 7 days must be excluded or D7 is unmeasurable
table choice on this question flips run to run - the known non-determinism case

questions.question: What is ARPU in between the month of may and june?

review.denominator: all active users in the period, not payers
traps: no year is given - the year must be resolved from the data, per tenant, and only a year holding BOTH months is valid
one row per month unless a combined total was asked for
the numerator is all revenue in the window - do not apply the activity filter to it

questions.question: What is the average session length by platform?

traps: fact_sessions stores session_duration_sec - do not derive it from the two timestamps
no period is stated, so window columns are what tell the reader what it covers

questions.question: What is ARPPU for the last 7 days?

review.denominator: distinct PAYING users only - this is what separates ARPPU from ARPU
traps: must not divide by all active users
fact_user_daily carries revenue_iap_usd and is_payer, so it answers this with no join at all - that is the better answer, not a miss

questions.question: How many new payers were there in the month of may?

review.denominator: none - this is a count, not a ratio
traps: 'new' means first-ever purchase, so a per-user MIN(event_date) is required
COUNT(*) over a per-user CTE is correct; COUNT(*) after joining back to a per-day table is not
the year must be resolved from the data and the month filter must not be left unbounded by year

questions.question: How many sessions per DAU did we have yesterday?

review.denominator: distinct active users on that day
traps: must not SUM a daily distinct count across days

questions.question: What is the tutorial completion rate by platform for the last 14 days?

review.denominator: users who STARTED the tutorial, not installs
traps: narrower than FTUE drop-off, which spans the wider onboarding path
any step-name string is a guessed value and should appear under review
